events.title: The election of Pope Adrian VI
events.shortBlurb: The cardinals unexpectedly chose a Dutch reformer, the last non-Italian pope until the twentieth century…
body: On 9 January 1522 the conclave, deadlocked among its factions, unexpectedly elected the absent Adrian of Utrecht, a Dutch theologian and former tutor of the emperor Charles V, who took the name Adrian VI. He was in Spain at the time and reached Rome only months later.

An austere and earnest man, he came to office determined to reform the Roman Curia and to answer the Lutheran revolt by acknowledging the Church's own need of correction, but his short reign of scarcely a year met resistance and ended with his death in 1523. He was the last non-Italian pope until the election of John Paul II in 1978.
